Authors: Scaife et al., CryptoLock (and Drop It)
Problem: Early ransomware file encryption on local filesystems
Method: File entropy, extension change rate, I/O bursts
KeyResults: 100% detection on test dataset; <10 files lost
Limitations: Local filesystem only; ignores cloud storage

Authors: Continella et al., ShieldFS
Problem: Low-level driver file system encryption rollback
Limitations: Kernel driver overhead; not suited for cloud multi-tenant VMs

Authors: Sgandurra et al., EldeRan
Problem: Automated dynamic feature analysis
Method: Dynamic API calls, registry, Regularized Logistic Regression
Limitations: Offline batch sandbox; not streaming real-time

Authors: Bae et al., ML Based on API & File Events
Problem: Distinguishing benign disk activity from fast cryptors
Limitations: Relies on API logs only; misses S3/Blob storage anomalies

Authors: Cabaj & Mazurczyk, SDN Ransomware Mitigation
Problem: Command & Control (C2) key exchange interception
Method: SDN OpenFlow controller inspecting HTTP/DNS C2
Limitations: Fails against modern offline/pre-bundled key ransomware

Authors: Davies et al., CloudRanger
Problem: Cloud virtual machine disk volume encryption
Method: 1D-CNN and LSTM on sequential disk I/O
Limitations: Heavy deep learning compute; no model explainability (SHAP)

Authors: Alhawi et al., ML for Windows Ransomware Traffic
Problem: Network anomaly detection of encryption propagation
Limitations: High false positives on cloud bulk sync / compression

Authors: Al-Rimawi et al., Comparative Study for Ransomware
Problem: Benchmarking ML classifiers on dynamic features
Method: Random Forest, SVM, KNN, AdaBoost, MLP
Limitations: No anomaly detector for novel zero-day patterns

Authors: Zahoora et al., Deep learning dynamic detection
Problem: Multi-stage ransomware with delayed encryption
Method: Autoencoder + Bi-LSTM on sliding time windows
Limitations: Long sequence observation window; high inference latency

Authors: Kok et al., RanCross Feature Extraction
Problem: Cross-platform Windows & Linux malware
Limitations: Offline evaluation; no cloud API/audit log integration

Authors: Kharaz et al., UNVEIL
Problem: Detecting silent lockers and desktop lockers
Method: Synthetic desktop environment and I/O monitor
KeyResults: High detection fidelity across widespread families
Limitations: Heavy desktop GUI requirements; useless for headless cloud VMs

Authors: Nguyen et al., Cloud-Guard
Problem: Hypervisor disk spikes and anomalous process spawning
Limitations: Pure anomaly detection; lacks supervised pattern discrimination

Authors: Biggio et al., Poisoning Attacks against SVMs
Problem: Gradient-based training data poisoning
KeyResults: Error increased from 3% to 24% with 8% poison
Limitations: Proved ML vulnerability; no automated defense pipeline

Authors: Jagielski et al., Manipulating Machine Learning
Problem: Poisoning attacks on regression and classification
Limitations: Assumes linear models; fails on tree ensembles

Authors: Shafahi et al., Poison Frogs! Targeted Clean-Label
Problem: Injecting poisoned inputs without label modification
Limitations: Label checks alone fail; feature outlier detection is required

Authors: Chen et al., Activation Clustering
Problem: Detecting poisoned backdoor clusters
Limitations: Restricted to DNNs; does not address tabular cloud security

Authors: Paudice et al., Label-Sanitization & k-NN
Problem: Filtering label-flipping and adversarial outliers
Method: k-NN consistency voting and distance thresholds
KeyResults: Filtered >90% label flips with <3% false quarantine
Limitations: Evaluated on static datasets; not integrated into retraining pipeline

Authors: Koh & Liang, Influence Functions
Problem: Finding training samples that alter model decisions
Limitations: Quadratic complexity; too slow for streaming retraining

Authors: Severi et al., Backdoor Attacks against Malware Classifiers
Problem: Exploiting SHAP explanations to craft backdoors
Limitations: Proves ML security models will fail without training data validation

Authors: Steinhardt et al., Certified Defenses for Poisoning
Problem: Upper bounds on test loss under data poisoning
Limitations: Requires convex losses rarely met in real cyber telemetry

Authors: Chen et al., Targeted Backdoor Attacks
Problem: Backdoor triggers activated only upon specific keys
Method: Targeted trigger injection into training subset
KeyResults: 99% trigger activation with clean test performance
Limitations: Emphasizes need for outlier screening + validation gating

Authors: Nicolae et al., Adversarial Robustness Toolbox
Problem: Standardizing adversarial attack & defense tools
Method: Library with label-flipping and LOF defenses
Limitations: Toolbox library only; not an end-to-end security system

Authors: Liu et al., Trojaning Attack on Neural Networks
Problem: Modifying internal weights using synthetic trojan data
Limitations: Requires model training access; reinforces validation gating

Authors: Cretu et al., Casting Out Demons
Problem: Preventing attacker from training anomaly sensors
KeyResults: Prevented sensor blinding by up to 95%
Limitations: Payload heuristics; lacks modern cloud telemetry and ML

Authors: Chiba et al., Real-time ML Architecture for Audit Logs
Problem: Detecting privilege escalation and account hijacking
Method: Spark Streaming and Random Forest on windowed metrics
Limitations: Focuses only on IAM; ignores disk entropy and ransomware encryption

Authors: Pour & Injadat, Streaming Intrusion Detection in Cloud
Problem: Concept drift adaptation in cloud NIDS
Method: Hoeffding Trees and Adaptive Random Forests
Limitations: Vulnerable to poisoning drift contaminating decision boundaries

Authors: Mirsky et al., Kitsune Online NIDS
Problem: Lightweight anomaly detection on streaming packets
Limitations: Unsupervised only; false alarms on benign high-volume bursts

Authors: Sommer & Paxson, Outside the Closed World
Problem: Fundamental gap between academic ML and operational security
Method: Qualitative analysis of false alarms and concept drift
Limitations: Proves pure anomaly detection is inadequate without hybrid classifiers
